(**A bacterial toxin has been licensed for reducing wrinkles since 2002. In the treatment, small amounts of the weakened toxin are injected into facial muscles. The toxin binds to presynaptic membranes of neuromuscular junctions, preventing synaptic vesicles from fusing with the presynaptic membranes. The toxin can reduce wrinkles for 3(4 months and the effect wears off. If the injections are placed improperly or the doses are incorrect, side effects such as droopy eyelids may develop.
a	Explain how the toxin can reduce wrinkles by acting on neuromuscular junctions.												(3 marks)
b	Suggest two causes of the loss of the effect of the toxin after a few months.															(2 marks)
a	The toxin prevents synaptic vesicles from fusing with the presynaptic membrane, and thus no neurotransmitter can be released to the synaptic clefts when nerve impulses arrive.												1m
Without the binding of neurotransmitter to the receptors on the postsynaptic membranes, electrical impulses cannot be generated by the muscle fibres of the facial muscles.												1m
The facial muscles cannot contract and wrinkles are therefore reduced.	1m
b	The toxin is destroyed by the immune system of the body.				1m

(**Read the following article and answer the questions.

A muscle relaxant is a drug which affects the function of skeletal muscles. There are two groups of muscle relaxants: the peripherally-acting relaxants and the centrally-acting relaxants, which are defined according to their sites of actions.

The peripherally-acting relaxants act by interfering with the transmission of nerve impulses at neuromuscular junctions. As they do not affect the central nervous system, they are often used in surgeries and emergency conditions to cause paralysis temporarily. The centrally-acting relaxants are mainly used to relieve muscle pain and cramps (non-coordinated contractions of a group of muscles).
a	Suggest one possible way in which the peripherally-acting relaxants cause paralysis.												(2 marks)
b	State one possible site where the centrally-acting relaxants may act on when they are used to relieve muscle pain and cramps respectively.	(2 marks)

c	Fruits of some plants contain substances whose chemical structure is similar to that of muscle relaxants. These fruits are toxic and often kill people who eat them. Explain how these fruits can kill.					(2 marks)
a	It destroys the neurotransmitter released by the ending of axons. 		1m
The muscle fibres therefore cannot be stimulated to generate electrical impulses that trigger muscle contractions. 								1m
Even when nerve impulses stimulate the release of neurotransmitter from the ending of axons, no electrical impulses are generated by the muscle fibres.	1m
b	To relieve muscle pain: sensory neurones in the spinal cord				1m
To relieve cramps: motor neurones in the spinal cord					1m
c	The substances in these fruits can block the transmission of nerve impulses at the neuromuscular junctions in the intercostal muscles.					1m
This can stop the breathing process and cause death.					1m
